judged_text: In deleteEvent the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only executes when externalCalendarId is falsy, and then searches for an entry whose externalId equals that falsy value — it can never match, so calendarId becomes undefined where the old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Cancelling a booking whose BookingReference row predates externalCalendarId storage (legacy rows written before this change) passes undefined as calendarId to calendar.events.delete; the deletion errors instead of removing the event, leaving orphaned calendar events on the destination calendar that can never be cleaned up through the app.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `deleteEvent` now computes `calendarId` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the fallback path), it then searches for a destination calendar whose `externalId` equals that same falsy value (e.g., `undefined`/`null`), which will not match a real externalId, resulting in `calendarId` being `undefined`. The old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (single value), but after the refactor to an array there is no equivalent fallback here (e.g., first destination calendar). Call sites like `handleCancelBooking.ts` pass `externalCalendarId` from booking references, which can plausibly be missing for legacy references, triggering this bad fallback and causing deletion to target an undefined calendar id instead of the intended destination calendar.
